label: Change in annual new CBHI enrollment
description: How much the annual rate of new CBHI enrollment changes relative to the baseline. The coverage expansion scenario in the study doubles annual enrollment, from about 685,000 to 1.37 million households, which corresponds to +100% on this slider.

label: Change in annual new fee-waiver beneficiaries
description: How much the annual rate of new fee-waiver enrollment changes relative to the baseline. The coverage expansion scenario doubles the number of households granted waivers each year, from about 12,000 to 24,000, which corresponds to +100% on this slider.

label: Reimbursement payment delay
description: How long facilities wait to be reimbursed for CBHI claims, shown in months. The baseline is 12 months. The CBHI reimbursement scenario halves this to 6 months. Moving the slider left shortens the delay; moving it right lengthens it. The shortest delay available is 1 month.

label: Change in reimbursement approval rate
description: How much the share of CBHI claims approved for payment changes relative to the baseline of 57%. The CBHI reimbursement scenario raises approval to 90%, which corresponds to +33% on this slider. The maximum setting brings approval to 100%.

label: Change in NCD screening rate
description: How much the rate of screening for hypertension and diabetes changes relative to the baseline. The screening promotion scenario doubles screening for both conditions, which corresponds to +100% on this slider. A negative value represents reduced screening activity.

label: Change in providers per facility
description: How much the target number of clinical providers per facility changes relative to the baseline of 2. The provider scenario raises the target to 3, which corresponds to +50% on this slider. Providers accumulate toward the target over time rather than changing immediately.

label: Change in provider productivity
description: How much of a provider's time is available for patient care, relative to the baseline of 57%. The remaining time is lost to training, official travel, and leave. The provider scenario raises availability to 80%, which corresponds to +23% on this slider. The maximum setting brings availability to 100%.

label: Change in facility medicine restocking rate
description: How much the rate at which facilities restock essential medicines changes relative to the baseline. The medicine availability scenario doubles the restocking rate, which corresponds to +100% on this slider. At the minimum setting restocking stops entirely.

label: Share of unutilized revenue used for medicines
description: The share of facility revenue that goes unspent each year and is redirected to purchasing essential medicines. The baseline is 0%, meaning no redirection. The medicine availability scenario redirects 50%. This is modeled as a hypothetical pathway rather than current practice.
